cards.title: Introduction to Flask Project Structure
cards.content:
As a Flask application grows, keeping all your code in a single app.py file becomes unmaintainable. A scalable Flask application uses a structured layout separating configuration, routes, models, and static assets.

We typically achieve this modularity by using the Application Factory pattern and Flask Blueprints.

content.question: What is the primary benefit of using the Application Factory pattern in Flask?

options.text: It automatically generates a database schema.
It allows you to create multiple instances of the app with different configurations.
It compiles Python bytecode into machine code for faster routing.
It eliminates the need for HTML templates.

cards.title: Standard Directory Layout
cards.content:
A production-ready Flask project often looks like this:

my_flask_app/
│
├── instance/
│   └── config.py
├── app/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── models.py
│   ├── static/
│   ├── templates/
│   └── main/
│       ├── __init__.py
│       └── routes.py
├── tests/
├── .env
├── requirements.txt
└── run.py

cards.title: Modularizing with Blueprints
cards.content:
Blueprints allow you to organize your Flask application into distinct components. Instead of registering all routes on the main application object, a blueprint records operations to be executed when registered on an application.

from flask import Blueprint

main_bp = Blueprint('main', __name__)

@main_bp.route('/')
def index():
    return 'Hello from the Blueprint!'

content.instructions: Put the steps of creating and running a structured Flask app in the correct order.

items.text: Create the application factory function inside app/__init__.py
Initialize extensions (like SQLAlchemy) inside the factory
Register your Blueprints to the app instance
Import and call the factory function in run.py to start the server

content.text:
Complete the basic application factory function in Python:

```python
from flask import Flask

def create_app(config_name=None):
    app = Flask(__name__)
    
    if config_name:
        app.config.from_object(config_name)
        
    # Register blueprint
    from app.main.routes import main_bp
    app.______(main_bp)
    
    return app
```
